answer: Trust propagation over the endorsement graph caps how many seats a farm can fund. Each epoch the protocol starts short random walks from jade seats, long-established agents picked by a public beacon, along that epoch's fresh endorsement edges. A farm forms a lagoon: dense inside but joined to honest agents by few edges, so walks rarely enter and its fakes split one small trust total. A gale of new walks reruns every epoch, so each extra fake needs its own new edge from an honest agent, who loses trust if it endorses junk.
